hero.title: About GenGrowth

minimalInput.title: Minimal Input First

abTest.title: A/B Test Sample Size Calculator
abTest.description: Calculate the required sample size for your A/B test based on baseline conversion rate, minimum detectable effect, and statistical parameters.
abTest.pageSubtitle: Calculate the required sample size for statistically significant A/B test results.
abTest.step1: Enter your current conversion rate as the baseline
abTest.step2: Set the minimum improvement you want to detect
abTest.step3: Choose your statistical confidence level and review the results
abTest.faq1q: What is a good sample size for an A/B test?
abTest.faq1a: It depends on your baseline conversion rate and the effect you want to detect. Use this calculator with your actual numbers for an accurate estimate.
abTest.faq2a: MDE is the smallest relative improvement in conversion rate that your test can reliably detect. A 20% MDE means you want to detect at least a 20% relative lift.
abTest.faq3q: How long should I run my A/B test?
abTest.faq3a: Divide the total sample size by your daily traffic. Most tests need 2-4 weeks for reliable results.

roi.step2: Add your team's manual growth work hours and cost
roi.step3: Review the projected savings and ROI from automation
roi.faq1q: How accurate is this ROI estimate?
roi.faq1a: This calculator uses industry averages for automation efficiency (70% time reduction, 15% conversion improvement). Actual results vary based on your product and implementation.
roi.faq2q: What costs does the ROI calculation include?
roi.faq2a: It includes time savings from reduced manual work and projected revenue from conversion improvements, compared against the cost of GenGrowth.
roi.faq3q: What is the assumed conversion improvement?
roi.faq3a: The calculator assumes a 15% relative improvement in conversion rate, which is a conservative estimate based on growth automation benchmarks.

seoAudit.metaTitle: Free SEO Audit & Website Health Map -- GenGrowth
seoAudit.metaDescription: Run a fast, evidence-led single-page SEO check covering crawlability, technical signals, on-page basics, extractability, and static structured data.
seoAudit.pageTitle: See the SEO signals search engines can actually read
seoAudit.pageSubtitle: A fast website health map built from the submitted page, robots.txt, and sitemap.xml. Every result shows its evidence, weighted coverage, and limits.
seoAudit.heroTrust: No login or site ownership check. We read one public page and its two standard support files.
seoAudit.scopeShort: Checks one public page plus robots.txt and sitemap.xml. No login, Search Console data, persistence, or full-site crawl.

errors.payload_too_large: The request is larger than this tool accepts.
errors.unsupported_media_type: This request format is not supported.
errors.scan_failed: We could not scan this site right now. Check that it is publicly reachable and try again.
errors.scan_timeout: The site did not respond within this preview's time limit.
errors.scan_in_progress: A scan from this network is already running. Wait a moment and try again.

seoAudit.summaryWithPriority: Start with {priority}. This run measured {percent}% of the weighted evidence.
seoAudit.summaryWithoutPriority: No measured fail or warning signals surfaced in this preview. This run measured {percent}% of the weighted evidence.
seoAudit.scopeBadge: 1 public page · no GSC · no crawl
seoAudit.coverage: Measurement coverage {percent}% · {measured} / {total} checks · site coverage: 1 URL
seoAudit.scoreDisclaimer: This is not a website health, ranking, or full-site score.
seoAudit.stageObservationBody: The public page response and two standard support files were read within fixed safety limits.
seoAudit.stageDiagnosisBody: {attention} measured signals need attention; unverified signals stay outside the diagnosis.
seoAudit.stageRecommendationBody: The repair sequence below shows the first {priorities} actionable items.
seoAudit.stageArtifactBody: Use the evidence map as the reproducible record for this single URL.
seoAudit.priorityListBody: Ordered by the audit's existing severity and weight. This public preview shows the first three.
seoAudit.noPriorities: No measured fail or warning signals surfaced. Review coverage and unverified evidence before treating the page as healthy.
seoAudit.diagnosisText: The observed evidence produced a {status} result for this signal.
seoAudit.verificationText: Publish the change, rerun this URL, and compare the same observed evidence.
seoAudit.signalMapBody: Compare score, evidence coverage, and status distribution across five modules. Expand a row for the observed evidence and next step.

page_status.title: Submitted-page response
page_status.recommendation: Restore a successful 200 response for the submitted page before optimizing other signals.

indexability.title: Indexability directive
indexability.recommendation: Remove unintended noindex directives from pages that should appear in search.

robots_access.title: Googlebot robots access
robots_access.recommendation: Keep robots.txt readable and remove unintended rules that block Googlebot from the submitted path.

sitemap.title: XML sitemap
sitemap.recommendation: Publish a valid XML sitemap at /sitemap.xml containing canonical, indexable URLs.

https.title: HTTPS delivery
https.recommendation: Serve the canonical site over HTTPS and redirect HTTP traffic to it.

redirects.title: Redirect path
redirects.recommendation: Link directly to the final URL and remove avoidable redirect hops.

html_content_type.title: HTML response type
html_content_type.recommendation: Return the page as HTML so search crawlers can parse its document-level signals.

canonical.title: Canonical alignment
canonical.recommendation: Declare one self-referencing canonical URL using the final HTTPS host and page path.

html_lang.title: HTML language
html_lang.recommendation: Set a valid lang attribute on the html element for the page language.

viewport.title: Mobile viewport
viewport.recommendation: Add a viewport meta tag with width=device-width and initial-scale=1 before testing rendered mobile layouts.

meta_refresh.title: HTML refresh redirect
meta_refresh.recommendation: Replace HTML refresh redirects with an appropriate server-side redirect or a direct canonical link.

security_headers.title: Security header presence
security_headers.recommendation: Review the missing transport and browser-protection headers; this preview checks only their presence, not policy quality.

title.title: Title tag
title.recommendation: Write one descriptive, page-specific title of roughly 30 to 60 characters.

meta_description.title: Meta description
meta_description.recommendation: Add a specific description that explains the page value in about 70 to 160 characters.

h1.title: Primary heading
h1.recommendation: Use one clear H1 that states the page's primary topic.

heading_order.title: Heading hierarchy
heading_order.recommendation: Keep heading levels sequential so crawlers and assistive technology can follow the structure.

text_depth.title: Static text extractability
text_depth.recommendation: Expose enough useful main content in crawlable HTML to explain the product, audience, and outcome.

social_meta.title: Social preview metadata
social_meta.recommendation: Add complete Open Graph and Twitter Card metadata for reliable shared previews.

json_ld.title: Static JSON-LD evidence
json_ld.recommendation: Validate the rendered page with a rich-results tool; add accurate schema only if it is truly absent.

limitations.standard_path_only: Only /sitemap.xml was checked. Another sitemap may be declared elsewhere.
limitations.static_html_cannot_prove_rendered_absenc: The raw response cannot prove that JavaScript-rendered structured data is absent.
limitations.projection_limit_reached: The bounded JSON-LD projection limit was reached, so later blocks were not evaluated.
limitations.response_body_truncated: The response exceeded the bounded read, so absence and complete counts were not inferred.
limitations.response_decode_unreliable: The response could not be decoded as declared or valid UTF-8, so document checks were not inferred.
limitations.html_body_unavailable: The response was not identifiable as an HTML document.
limitations.resource_fetch_unavailable: The standard resource could not be measured in this run.
limitations.resource_decode_unreliable: The standard resource could not be decoded reliably in this run.
limitations.https_required_for_hsts: Security-header presence is not separately assessed on HTTP because HSTS only applies after HTTPS is enabled.

seoAudit.howIntro: One submitted public URL becomes a bounded repair brief. The check names what it measured and what it could not safely infer.
seoAudit.step1Text: The URL and every redirect are checked against private and reserved network ranges.
seoAudit.step2Text: We read the submitted page, robots.txt, and sitemap.xml with strict time and response-size limits.
seoAudit.step3Text: Unverified checks stay outside the score and every actionable result keeps its observed evidence.
seoAudit.signalsEyebrow: Read the result with its limits
seoAudit.signalsTitle: What each part of the health map tells you
seoAudit.signalsBody: The map separates measurable signals from assumptions, so a missing or incomplete response does not turn into a confident-looking recommendation.
seoAudit.signal1Body: Response status, noindex directives, Googlebot access to the submitted path, and the standard sitemap path.
seoAudit.signal2Body: The final protocol, redirect chain, content type, canonical URL, language, viewport, HTML refresh, and selected security-header presence.
seoAudit.signal3Body: The static title, meta description, H1 count, and heading hierarchy seen in the fetched response.
seoAudit.signal4Body: Static text depth and social metadata—not a judgment of content quality, search intent, or site structure.
seoAudit.signal5Body: Closed JSON-LD blocks visible in the raw response. JavaScript-rendered markup remains explicitly unverified.
seoAudit.useCasesEyebrow: When a fast check is useful
seoAudit.useCasesTitle: Use this as a first, evidence-led pass
seoAudit.useCasesBody: It is built for a concrete URL and a concrete next action—not for claiming that a whole domain is healthy.
seoAudit.useCase1Body: Confirm the public response, canonical basics, and static on-page signals before you ask search engines to revisit it.
seoAudit.useCase2Title: When a page looks unexpectedly hard to find
seoAudit.useCase2Body: Check the measurable crawl and indexation signals first, then use deeper tools only where the evidence points.
seoAudit.useCase3Body: Get a bounded baseline for one URL; use the result to decide whether multi-page crawling or rendered evidence is needed.
seoAudit.methodTransparencyTitle: How the health map reaches a finding
seoAudit.method1Title: Measure the same bounded sources every time
seoAudit.method1Body: The submitted page, its final same-origin robots.txt, and the standard sitemap.xml are the only V0 inputs. The tool does not silently add a crawl.
seoAudit.method2Body: Every status carries stable evidence labels and sources. A recommendation can be reviewed against what the scanner actually observed.
seoAudit.method3Body: A truncated, non-HTML, unavailable, or unreliably decoded response becomes unverified where appropriate, rather than creating a false pass or fail.
seoAudit.limitsTitle: What this preview will not tell you
seoAudit.limit1Title: Whether Google has indexed the page
seoAudit.limit1Body: The audit reads technical signals that can affect indexability. It cannot observe Google’s index, crawl scheduling, or Search Console data.
seoAudit.limit2Title: What JavaScript adds after the raw response
seoAudit.limit2Body: Static markup can confirm what is present, but it cannot prove that rendered metadata, links, or JSON-LD are absent.
seoAudit.limit3Title: Whether the rest of the site is healthy
seoAudit.limit3Body: A one-page result is a repair starting point. It is not a full crawl, performance assessment, backlink analysis, or content-quality verdict.
seoAudit.comparison1Title: When a single-page check is the right first step
seoAudit.comparison1Body: Use it when you need a fast, reproducible answer about a page you are publishing, repairing, or investigating before spending time on a deeper audit.
seoAudit.comparison2Title: When to move to a full Website Audit
seoAudit.comparison2Body: Use the full product when the evidence points beyond one URL: multi-page relationships, rendered output, performance evidence, history, and a managed repair queue.
seoAudit.ctaTitle: Need the whole site, not one page?
seoAudit.ctaBody: GenGrowth's full Website Audit adds multi-page crawling, rendered evidence, performance data, history, and an execution-ready fix queue.
seoAudit.faq1q: Is this a complete SEO audit?
seoAudit.faq1a: No. It is a fast static check of one submitted page plus robots.txt and sitemap.xml. It does not claim full-site, ranking, backlink, Search Console, or browser-rendered coverage.
seoAudit.faq2q: Why can structured data show as not verified?
seoAudit.faq2a: Many sites inject JSON-LD with JavaScript. A static fetch can confirm markup it sees, but it cannot safely prove that rendered markup is absent.
seoAudit.faq3q: Does a high score guarantee rankings?
seoAudit.faq3a: No. The score summarizes only measured technical and on-page signals. Search demand, content quality, competition, authority, and actual indexation require additional evidence.
seoAudit.faq4q: Is the Website Health Map free, and do I need to sign in?
seoAudit.faq4a: This public preview is free and does not require a login or proof of site ownership. It is rate-limited to protect the service and does not save a project or scan history.
seoAudit.faq5q: How should I interpret the score and coverage?
seoAudit.faq5a: The score uses only checks that were actually measured. Coverage shows how much weighted evidence was available; unverified checks are excluded rather than being treated as passing or failing.
seoAudit.faq6q: Does the robots.txt check prove that Google can crawl my whole site?
seoAudit.faq6a: No. It evaluates Googlebot rules for the submitted URL path in the fetched robots.txt. It does not prove discovery, crawl budget, rendering, or indexing across the rest of the site.
seoAudit.faq7q: Why might a check be unverified?
seoAudit.faq7a: A support file may be unavailable, the response may be non-HTML, truncated, or not safely decodable, or a signal may only exist after JavaScript runs. The report names that boundary instead of guessing.
seoAudit.faq8q: What changes in the full GenGrowth Website Audit?
seoAudit.faq8a: The full product can add multi-page crawling, rendered evidence, performance data, history, and an execution-ready fix queue. Those capabilities are outside this anonymous, one-page preview.
seoAudit.relatedToolsBody: Each public tool answers one bounded question. Browse the collection when the next question goes beyond this URL's technical response.
seoAudit.articlesBody: Read the programmatic SEO guide for the site architecture and implementation questions that a single-page check intentionally leaves open.

faq1.q: Can GenGrowth fully replace a growth team?
faq1.a: GenGrowth automates the operational aspects of growth marketing -- strategy generation, content creation, multi-channel execution, and optimization. For early-stage teams or solo operators, it can serve as the primary growth engine. Larger organizations may use it to augment their existing team.

faq2.q: How quickly can I see results after switching from manual growth?
faq2.a: Most users see their first automated strategies generated within minutes of setup. Execution results typically begin appearing within 1-2 weeks. The optimization loop becomes more effective over time as the system accumulates performance data.

faq3.q: What happens if I want to customize the AI-generated strategies?
faq3.a: GenGrowth generates strategies as proposals that you can review, approve, modify, or reject before execution. You maintain full control. The system learns from your approval patterns to better align future strategies with your preferences.

faq1.q: Are link exchanges risky for SEO?
faq1.a: Google's guidelines explicitly warn against link schemes including reciprocal link exchanges at scale. A 2,500-site link exchange network could trigger algorithmic or manual penalties. GenGrowth uses white-hat link building strategies that align with search engine guidelines.

faq2.a: BabyLoveGrowth delivers a fixed package of 30 articles, link exchanges, and Reddit posts per month. There is no discovery phase, no strategy framework, and no optimization based on results. GenGrowth builds strategies based on your specific product, market, and performance data.

faq3.q: Can BabyLoveGrowth attribute results to specific actions?
faq3.a: No. BabyLoveGrowth does not include attribution tracking. You cannot determine which articles, links, or Reddit posts drove traffic or conversions. GenGrowth attributes every result to its source strategy and channel.
